title: Telemetry Evidence Automation & Connector Blueprint
content:
Purpose and scope:

This blueprint captures a pragmatic, customer-facing specification for shipping telemetry and evidence artifacts from Redwood Inference to common SIEMs (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, Microsoft Sentinel / Log Analytics). It focuses on three correlated concerns: 1) audit log schema and RBAC v2 event surface; 2) evidence automation (how evidence files and artifact metadata are produced, hashed, and exported); and 3) connector operational requirements (network, throughput, retries, data shaping, privacy). Audience: engineering (integrations), security/compliance, and customer onboarding/solutions teams.

Goals:
- Provide a single, reviewable spec customers can use to approve outbound telemetry contracts and firewall requirements.
- Define a stable audit event schema aligned with RBAC v2 entitlement changes, permission checks, and high-fidelity evidence pointers.
- Give connector implementers clear examples for Splunk, Datadog, and Microsoft Sentinel ingestion: headers, batching guidance, idempotency, and error-handling patterns.
- Define redaction & minimization rules and automated evidence retention controls required for compliance.

Non-goals:
- Full implementation guide for customer-side SIEM configuration.
- Proprietary SDK code; samples are protocol-level.

1) RBAC v2 -> Audit event mapping

Summary: RBAC v2 introduces scoped roles, resource tags, and delegated namespaces. Each API authorization decision must generate a single audit event that contains: actor, action, resource, scope, decision, policy_id, and policy_evaluation_summary. Connector consumers must be able to reconstruct who did what, where, and why.

Minimum event fields (required):
- event_id: string (UUID v4)
- timestamp: string (RFC 3339)
- actor_id: string (internal user id or service principal)
- actor_type: string (user|service|system)
- action: string (e.g., token.create, model.deploy, audit.log.export)
- resource_type: string (project|model|dedicated-pool|deployment)
- resource_id: string
- scope: string (global|org:ORG_ID|project:PROJ_ID|namespace:NAMESPACE)
- decision: string (allow|deny|conditional)
- policy_id: string (RBAC_v2 policy identifier)
- policy_evaluation: string (short summary, or reference id to full evaluation blob)
- request_id: string (correlation id for RPC tracing)
- client_ip: string (ipv4/ipv6)
- user_agent: string
- evidence_ref: string (optional pointer to evidence artifact)
- outcome_metadata: string (freeform; e.g., rate-limited, fallback-triggered)

Note on optional fields: evidence_ref is present when the action generates artifacts (uploads, downloads, attestation generation). The connector must preserve and export the evidence_ref verbatim so downstream auditors can retrieve matching evidence bundles.

2) Audit event JSON example (single-line JSON to ease ingestion):
{
  "event_id": "3f8e2b9a-1f6a-4b3e-b9a7-4c2f0a8b6d9a",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-21T15:23:45.123Z",
  "actor_id": "u_7c4d2f",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "action": "model.deploy",
  "resource_type": "model",
  "resource_id": "m_rlhf_v2:2026-01-20",
  "scope": "org:acme-corp",
  "decision": "allow",
  "policy_id": "rbacv2-policy-13",
  "policy_evaluation": "eval-7c9a",
  "request_id": "req-2a8b9c",
  "client_ip": "203.0.113.45",
  "user_agent": "redwood-cli/0.18.1",
  "evidence_ref": "evidence:bundle:2026-01-21:3f8e2b9a",
  "outcome_metadata": "autoscaled-to-dedicated-pool"
}

3) Evidence automation: artifact model and lifecycle

When an audited action produces an evidentiary artifact (model hashes, signed policy snapshots, customer-provided data extracts), Redwood will bundle artifacts into a signed evidence bundle and produce a minimal metadata record that is referenced from the audit event (evidence_ref).

Evidence bundle metadata (exported inline or as a lightweight companion record):
- evidence_id: string (UUID)
- created_at: RFC3339 string
- producer_service: string (e.g., inference-controlplane)
- artifacts: string (comma-separated short ids)
- artifact_hashes: string (comma-separated SHA256 hashes)
- signature: string (opaque base64 signature of the manifest)
- retention_days: string (numeric)
- access_policy: string (internal ACL ref or external entitlement pointer)
- download_url: string (signed URL or storage_ref)

Evidence handling rules for connectors:
- By default, connectors export the audit event and include evidence_ref. Connectors should NOT attempt to fetch large evidence bundles unless customer explicitly opts in.
- If customer opts in to evidence export, connector must fetch the evidence manifest only (not binary artifacts) and include the manifest as a compact JSON in the export payload under evidence_manifest. Binary artifacts must be referenced by signed download_url and stored in a customer-controlled S3/GCS or Redwood-controlled encrypted store depending on contract.
- All evidence manifests must include artifact_hashes and signature to allow downstream verification.

4) Connector protocol specifics

General guidance (applies to all endpoints):
- Events must be newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) unless the target SIEM requires a different envelope.
- Timestamps must be RFC3339 and in UTC.
- Include a top-level field: redwood_export_version: "v1" so consumers can evolve parsing.
- Use event batching with a target batch size of 100–500 events or 512KB per request, whichever comes first.
- Compression: gzip for payloads > 64KB.
- Idempotency: include sequence_id + first_event_id in batch metadata to enable de-duplication.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter; mark events failed only after 10 attempts total (3 immediate, then backoff windows up to 15 minutes).

Splunk HEC specifics:
- Endpoint: https://input-{region}.splunkcloud.com/services/collector/event
- Auth: HEC Token in Authorization header: "Splunk <token>"
- Indexing fields: send event as JSON with fields for sourcetype: "redwood:audit:rbacv2" and source: "redwood-inference" and host: optional customer hostname.
- When exporting evidence_manifest inline, set "metadata" object with evidence_id and download_url.
- HEC considerations: set "time" numeric field (epoch seconds) and avoid top-level arrays in event body.

Datadog Logs specifics:
- Endpoint: https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input
- Auth: DD-API-KEY header (customer-provided)
- Minimal fields: "ddsource": "redwood-inference", "service": "platform-controlplane", "hostname": optional, "ddtags": "env:prod,org:acme"
- Use "message" for freeform and a "attributes" map for structured fields. Single-line JSON recommended with top-level attribute "event_type".

Microsoft Sentinel / Log Analytics specifics:
Two supported patterns: 1) direct ingestion to Log Analytics Data Collector API (workspace ID/key); 2) push to Event Hub configured as Diagnostic Sink into Sentinel.
- Data Collector API: HTTP POST to https://{workspaceId}.ods.opinsights.azure.com/api/logs?api-version=2016-04-01 with Authorization header computed via workspace key. Payload: JSON array of records.
- For simplicity, prefer small batches (<= 64 records) to avoid throttling.
- Required property: "Type": "RedwoodAudit_RBACv2" in each record so Sentinel parsers can map fields.
- Event Hub pattern: send events as NDJSON; coordinate with customer on Event Hub partitioning keys (use org or project hash) to preserve ordering.

5) Privacy & redaction rules

Default redaction policy (applies unless customer signs DPA exception):
- PII elements (emails, SSNs, phone numbers) must be redacted from exported event fields. Use "[REDACTED_PII]" token.
- IP addresses: export client_ip only as /24 masked for IPv4 and /48 masked for IPv6 unless customer requests full IP in contract.
- Uploaded customer data snapshots: never export raw content by default. Export only metadata and evidence_manifest references.

Field-level redaction guidance for implementers:
- Replace values with deterministic token for correlation when redaction applied (e.g., actor_id -> redacted-<sha256(actor_id)[:8]>).
- Preserve event shape and field names to ensure SIEM parsers do not break.

6) Customer onboarding checklist (network & security)
- Decide ingestion pattern: Splunk HEC / Datadog / Sentinel (Event Hub or Log Analytics)
- Provide endpoint(s), auth tokens/keys, allowed CIDR ranges for Redwood outbound egress. If customer requires static IPs, engage SRE for egress pool allocation (lead time ~4 weeks).
- TLS required for all endpoints; mutual TLS supported for Splunk on-prem via customer configuration.
- Contractual: retention_days for evidence bundles and audit exports; default is 90 days for logs and 365 days for evidence manifests unless enterprise contract specifies otherwise.
- Data residency: confirm region; for EU customers, route to EU endpoints only.
- Privacy: confirm PII export allowances and masking rules; capture DPA appendix if different.

7) Operational checks and dashboards (SRE / Console)
- Per-customer export success rate (1h/24h/7d), avg latency, and latest failure reason.
- Per-customer queue depth and retry counts. Alert when queue depth exceeds threshold (default 10k events) or failure rate > 1% over 1h.
- Provide a "export-verification" runbook that: 1) lists most recent event_id exported; 2) fetches sample event from SIEM; 3) validates schema (required fields present); 4) validates evidence_ref resolves to manifest.

8) Parsing and detection recipes (sample queries)
- Splunk example: index=prod sourcetype="redwood:audit:rbacv2" action=model.deploy | stats count by decision, actor_type
- Datadog example: logs("service:platform-controlplane AND event_type:rbacv2").group_by(["decision"], "count()")
- Sentinel / KQL example: RedwoodAudit_RBACv2 | where action == "token.create" | summarize count() by actor_id

9) Versioning and evolution
- redwood_export_version is required in every exported payload. Current: v1. Future incompatible changes will be v2 and require explicit customer opt-in and 30-day notice.

10) Escalation and contacts
- Integration owner: asha.patel@redwood.ai
- Security lead: diego.martinez@redwood.ai
- SRE / egress setup: sres-oncall@redwood.ai

Appendix A: Example evidence_manifest JSON (compact)
{
  "evidence_id": "evi-9b1f8c",
  "created_at": "2026-01-21T15:23:46Z",
  "producer_service": "inference-controlplane",
  "artifacts": "model-hash,policy-snapshot",
  "artifact_hashes": "a3f5...e2b4,a4c2...d1f9",
  "signature": "MEUCIQDb...",
  "retention_days": "365",
  "access_policy": "acl:org:acme:security-team",
  "download_url": "https://redwood-evidence.storage/acme/evi-9b1f8c/manifest.json?sig=..."
}

Appendix B: Common failure modes and mitigation
- 401 Unauthorized: token rotation mismatch — refresh token and validate clock skew.
- 413 Payload too large: reduce batch size or enable payload compression.
- 429 Throttled by SIEM: implement per-customer backoff and exponential retry; notify customer about ingestion limits.
